question: What marks the very beginning of a patient's journey in a healthcare facility?
explanation: The patient journey officially starts at the point of first contact, which usually involves reception and registration at the facility. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is smooth coordination of the patient journey important in busy Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It prevents bottlenecks and reduces client anxiety
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for patient records
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid documentation duties
options.D: It guarantees that treatment will always be free

explanation: Good coordination keeps movement efficient, preventing overcrowding and helping patients feel safe and guided. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary effect of a warm and professional greeting on a newly arrived patient?

options.C: It builds trust and reduces anxiety
options.D: It replaces the need for vital signs

explanation: Greeting patients warmly helps them feel secure and lowers the fear often associated with hospital visits. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h2)

question: A woman arrives at the antenatal clinic looking distressed and confused. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Greet her calmly and offer a reassuring seat
options.B: Demand her hospital card before speaking to her
options.C: Ignore her until she approaches the desk herself
options.D: Tell her to go back outside until she is quiet

explanation: Calm, respectful initial engagement helps de-escalate distress and shows the patient she is welcome and safe. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is collected as part of biographical data during admission?

options.C: Next of kin and home address

explanation: Biographical data focuses on identifying information, including names, addresses, and emergency contact details. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of taking baseline vital signs upon admission?

options.A: To determine the exact date the patient will be discharged
options.B: To replace the need for a physical head-to-toe exam
options.C: To prove that the patient has paid their hospital fees
options.D: To provide a reference point for future clinical changes

explanation: Baseline vitals give nurses a starting measurement to compare against when checking for patient deterioration later. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h3)

question: When is an inter-facility patient referral primarily indicated?

options.A: When the nurse wants to reduce the ward workload
options.B: When visiting hours are about to close for the day
options.C: When the patient's needs exceed current facility capacity
options.D: When the patient simply dislikes the ward paint color

explanation: Referrals are safety measures used when a hospital lacks the equipment, specialists, or level of care required by the patient. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: What critical action must be taken before physically transporting an emergency referral patient?

options.A: Discharge all other patients in the ward
options.D: Wait for all relatives to pay cash deposits

explanation: Patients must be stabilized as much as possible before transit to prevent deterioration on the road. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: At what point in the hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?
explanation: Early discharge planning ensures enough time to prepare the patient and family for a smooth transition home. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h5)

question: A postnatal mother is preparing for discharge. What is the most important information the midwife must share with her?

options.A: A complete inventory of ward cleaning supplies
options.B: The history of how the hospital was built
options.C: The personal phone number of the hospital director
options.D: Danger signs that require returning to the hospital

explanation: Teaching danger signs helps the mother spot complications early and seek prompt medical help at home. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which body regulates the professional practice and conduct of midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Union of Road Transport Workers
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing and midwifery education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why is contemporaneous documentation legally crucial during patient admission and care?

options.A: It ensures the hospital wins every court case automatically
options.B: It allows nurses to skip giving oral handovers
options.C: It provides an accurate, timed record of care given
options.D: It replaces the need for any doctor's prescriptions

explanation: Recording events as they happen prevents memory lapses and serves as legal proof of the clinical care provided. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h6)
